faq.q: Can I make fashion video ads from a flat garment photo?
faq.a: Yes. Lay the garment flat or hang it on a plain wall, smooth out wrinkles, and photograph the whole piece in even light. Then describe the person and setting you want to show.

faq.q: Can I turn a photo of a garment laid flat into an on-model photo?
faq.a: Yes. Lay the garment flat or hang it on a plain wall, smooth out the wrinkles, and photograph the whole piece in even light. Then describe the person and setting, for example "full-length, standing in a bright studio."

faq.q: Will the AI change my print or fabric?
faq.a: It works from your photo, so fine stripes, embroidery, and buttons hold up when the upload is sharp and close. Check patterns and trims before you list the image, and make another version if anything drifts.

faq.q: Can I show my clothes on a plus-size or petite model?
faq.a: You can describe the person you want to see, including height, build, and age range, such as "petite woman in her 40s" or "tall man with a broad frame." Showing your real customer helps shoppers picture themselves in the piece.

faq.q: How do I make a TikTok video of my clothes being worn?
faq.a: Choose 9:16 and a length of 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds, then describe a slow turn or short walk. Run another version when you want a different setting.

faq.q: What photo works best for putting my garment on a model?
faq.a: Use a flat-lay or hanger shot with the whole garment visible, front side up and even light. The outline, color, print, and fastenings have to be clear because the generated model keeps those details.

faq.q: Can I show the same outfit as separate photo and video ads?
faq.a: Yes. One clear garment photo can produce a model photo and a short fit or turn video. Use the still for the listing or a square feed ad, and use the moving version for in-feed placements where the walk or turn shows the fit.

faq.q: How do I keep fabric color accurate?
faq.a: Shoot in soft daylight without a warm lamp, and name the color plainly, such as charcoal, ivory, or navy. Check the result against the real garment before publishing; if the tone drifts, generate another version.

faq.q: Can I run the clips as paid clothing ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloaded clips are watermark-free and licensed for commercial use, including paid social ads. Claims about sizing and fabric must match the real item, and the platform still reviews the ad.

faq.q: Is an AI model video different from a real UGC creator?
faq.a: Yes. The model and scene are generated from your photo at a per-clip credit cost instead of a creator fee and usage terms. The person is not a real customer, so post the video as an ad rather than an independent review.
